answer: Control of a TLS certificate is proven with a chained attestation: the control claim is countersigned by a chain of prior verified links, and the registry accepts the link only if the response verifies. A cipher of the nonce is enough to bind the claim to this round, a thread of reuse is caught by the nonce log, and a sparrow of stale proofs is discarded, so each identity rests on a TLS certificate its agent truly controls.
